messages:
sarah: Quick heads-up — our GCP invoice for us-west1 showed an effective committed GPU price increase ~14% vs last month. This is hitting Dedicated unit economics for the APAC-replicated pools. I pulled the billing delta and attached the short summary below.

mike: Can you paste the delta numbers here? rough % / $ per-GPU?

sarah: Sure — short version:
```
prev_effective_hourly: $1.92 per A100
new_effective_hourly:  $2.19 per A100
delta: +$0.27/hr (+14.1%)
estimated_monthly_impact: ~+$45k on committed pools (current utilization)
```

eli: Oof. Is this just a pricing tier change from the provider or a billing misclassification? Any credits/commitments that failed to apply?

sarah: I checked line items — looks like a regional SDD tax + new spot floor changes. Not a missing credit. Also saw a small change in egress tiering that bumped a few large copies.

julia-finance: Thanks for flagging. We need an updated margin check ASAP. What's the current gross margin on Dedicated after this hit?

mike: Ballpark before this was 34% on Dedicated (after infra op costs). With +14% GPU cost, that drops to ~27% assuming no pass-through. If we absorb, it goes below our target band.

diane: Two operational levers we can use quickly: 1) shift non-latency-critical customers from us-west1 -> us-central1 / europe-west4 where quotes are still lower, 2) throttle burst capacity (reduce autoscale headroom) for next 6 weeks. Both need customer comms / warnings.

eli: Rebalancing note: moving stateful workloads will incur ~5–10ms added RTT for some clients and extra egress charges for cross-region cache repopulation. For stateless batch/ranking work it's trivial.

julia-finance: Can we run a simulation: move 30% of Dedicated batch traffic to cheaper regions + reduce burst by 20% => what's the net monthly saving and impact to SLO? I can push a quick model if you give utilization numbers.

sarah: I mocked a quick calc: 30% region shift + 20% burst throttle -> ~-$28k/month on invoice delta, netting ~-$17k/month residual (vs original +$45k). SLO impact: maybe +1–3ms p50 for those clients, p99 unaffected if we keep canary.

mike: Sounds reasonable. Two asks before we act: 1) confirm spare capacity in target regions for the shift (eli), 2) update the unit-econ model and run the margin table (julia).

eli: Checked capacity: us-central1 has headroom for an initial 30% shift for next 30 days, but sustained -> talk to capacity planning. Also we should avoid shifting Dedicated customers that rely on pinned GPUs in us-west1 (list in the dashboard).

infra-bot: [deploy-notice] Canary route rule created: route 10% of traf to us-central1 for service redwood-dedicated-batch at 2026-03-18T16:20Z.

diane: Let's make the canary 10% initially for 48h, measure request latency, error rates, and costs. If stable, expand to 30% in weekly increments. Someone run the A/B dashboard check and add the cost delta to the ticket.

julia-finance: I'll update the unit economics sheet and push a new margin table by EOD. Link: https://sheets.internal/redwood/dedicated-margin-q2 (internal).

mike: Also we should open a cloud billing dispute/negotiation thread — 14% bump is material. @sarah can you start a support case and cc procurement? Note: ask for retroactive application of prior committed discounts where applicable.

sarah: On it. Opening ticket now. Draft note in case we need approval: "Request review of regional pricing deltas and application of committed usage discounts for Q1–Q2; ask for marketplace credits or transition guidance."

eli: Ops checklist: 1) run canary (10%) — done. 2) monitor p50/p95/p99 and error rates. 3) run cross-region egress estimate for cache warmup. I'll post results in this thread within 24h.

julia-finance: If the provider won't remedy, we should consider: 1) passing partial price increases to new Dedicated contracts, 2) pushing a temporary surcharge on heavy egress customers, or 3) accelerating Reserved renegotiation window with provider (procurement). I'll add scenarios to the sheet.

mike: Good. Let's avoid a surprise product message — ops-first approach. Diane, coordinate comms with CSMs for any customers impacted by region moves. Sarah, keep procurement looped on the ticket. Julia, send the updated margin table. I'll align on exec readout if numbers stay bad.

sarah: filing ticket + adding notes. will drop a summary here once ticket id is back. :thumbsup:

diane: I'll kick off the CSM heads-up email draft — short & opt-in for region move where possible.

mike: Thanks all. Action items recap (quick):
- sarah: open billing support ticket & report id (owner)
- eli: run canary metrics + egress estimate (owner)
- diane: CSM comms draft & opt-in plan (owner)
- julia-finance: updated unit-econ + margin scenarios EOD (owner)
- mike: exec summary if we need to escalate

sarah: noted. will post ticket id and a tight summary here when available.

infra-bot: [reminder] Follow-up: canary metrics check scheduled in 48h.

mike: Will revisit after canary metrics. Thanks everyone. :raised_hands:
